name: Treaty with the Choctaw, 1816 (Treaty of Fort St. Stephens)
aka: Treaty of the Choctaw Trading House
nations: Choctaw (Chahta) Nation, today the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma, the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians and the Jena Band of Choctaw Indians
promises: The Choctaw ceded their title to the lands east of a line down the Tombigbee from the mouth of the Ooktibbuha to the northern line of the 1805 Mount Dexter cession (Article 1).
The United States would pay the Choctaw $6,000 a year for twenty years (Article 2).
The United States would deliver $10,000 in merchandise on signing (Article 2).
landTaken: Royce Area 82 in present Alabama and Mississippi, the land east of the Tombigbee line in Article 1.
compensation: The treaty consideration was $6,000 a year for twenty years and $10,000 in merchandise (Article 2). Whether all twenty annuities were paid was not traced.
today: No Indian Claims Commission or court ruling on this cession was found. The Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma publishes the treaty text under the name 1816 Treaty of Fort St. Stephens.

nationVoice.summary: The Nation publishes the Kappler text of this treaty as the 1816 Treaty of Fort St. Stephens, without further commentary in that document.

sources.title: Treaty with the Choctaw, 1816 (Kappler, vol. 2, p. 137)
sources.publisher: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Tribal Treaties Database

openQuestions: Thirteen Choctaw decisions in the OSU ICC collection (Dockets 16, 51, 55, 56, 103 and 249) were searched for the 1816 treaty, 7 Stat. 152 and Royce Area 82 with no hit; the Commission's 1978 Final Report docket list was not checked.
Whether the twenty annual payments of $6,000 were all made was not researched.
No Choctaw account of what this cession meant to the nation was found beyond the published text.
